lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 18, which makes CI prove every pull request in a running Thunar.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
It starts from the build job, which already makes the PR's five debs.
The verify job installs three of them, plus the test tools, from a cache when it can.
A smoke test starts Thunar on a virtual display and checks it is still running after ten seconds.
lines.say: A smoke test starts Thunar on a virtual display, and checks it is still running after ten seconds.

lines.caption: Then each feature test script drives Thunar and takes before and after screenshots.
Every screenshot, and a manifest of them, is committed to the shots branch.
The verify section of the PR comment shows the results and each screenshot under its caption.
An agent audits the screenshots, and you review them and merge.
A cloud session may not be able to run Thunar, and a report saying it works proves nothing. So CI has to prove it.
The verify section is the proof, not an agent's report. Before you merge, look at the shots.
Steps one and two: verify waits for the build, then installs from the cache, and falls back to apt.
Step three gives the smoke test its own display, window manager and D-Bus session.
lines.say: Step three gives the smoke test its own display, window manager and D bus session.

lines.caption: Step four: each script gets a fresh home folder and at most two minutes, and a misnamed script fails the job.
Steps five and six publish the shots and write the verify section, even when a test failed.
Step seven: an independent auditor reads every screenshot and checks its caption.
The repo now carries a CLAUDE.md that cloud sessions read: branch rules, build lessons and the test contract.
Three screenshot skills are ported from another project, plus helpers each test script sources.
The deb cache, Zorin's theme in the shots, and image links pinned to the commit that added them.
Every test script gets its own display, home folder, work folder and shots folder, and two minutes.
The PR adds the verify job and its scripts, the repo's instructions, and the screenshot skills.
To turn verify off, delete its job from the workflow. Nothing else depends on it.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was tested with main's packages, copies the explainer job's pattern, and ports existing skills.
In a container set up like the runner, installing worked from an empty cache, a full one, and a broken one.
The smoke test passed in thirteen seconds, and four throwaway scripts exercised the test runner.
Publishing was dry-run, also with failing uploads, and the scripts passed the linters.
On the PR's first CI run, build, verify and explainer were green, and the audit passed the smoke shot.
On the third push, the cache hit: thirty-one debs installed in eleven seconds.
The billed Actions minutes of each job were also recorded.
A fresh local agent found six issues, one of them medium. All six were fixed and re-run.
CI's own review found more medium ones, like tests sharing one display. Those are fixed too.
Three low findings were accepted on purpose.
The shared cache, a real feature script, and the cloud sandbox can only be tried after the merge.
Part 3. What comes later: the sandbox check, the issue 3 trial, then issue 2.
Next comes a sandbox check, then an agent's trial PR for issue 3, then auto-deploy in issue 2.
A web session checks whether its own sandbox can build and run Thunar, and records what it finds.
Then an agent implements issue 3 with the first real test script, and its Actions minutes are recorded.
Finally, an updater installs each release, which only follows a proven, reviewed merge.
That's the tour: every PR now runs in a real Thunar under CI, and you see the screenshots before you merge.
